claims.text: A nickel-based superalloy with a well-defined gamma-prime precipitate microstructure will exhibit marked temperature-dependent plastic deformation.
Plasticity in the proposed superalloy is dislocation-controlled at room temperature.
Above approximately 600 °C, the superalloy will exhibit enhanced plastic flow.
Precipitate coarsening or dissolution causes the enhanced plastic flow at elevated temperatures.
The as-processed material contains a uniform distribution of gamma-prime precipitates.
Gamma-prime precipitate size, distribution, and stability mediate the temperature-dependent mechanical response.
At lower temperatures, gamma-prime precipitates hinder dislocation motion.
The hindrance of dislocation motion by gamma-prime precipitates provides high yield strength.
Increasing temperature causes gamma-prime precipitates to coarsen or partially dissolve.
Coarsening or partial dissolution reduces the precipitates' barrier effect on dislocations.
A reduced precipitate barrier increases dislocation mobility and plastic flow.
Yield strength will drop significantly beyond a critical temperature near 600 °C relative to room temperature.
Plastic strain or deformation rate will increase beyond a critical temperature near 600 °C relative to room temperature.
At room temperature, gamma-prime precipitates effectively impede dislocation motion.
The proposed behavior is expected only where oxidation and other high-temperature degradation mechanisms do not dominate.
The threshold temperature and magnitude of the mechanical changes depend on alloy composition, precipitate volume fraction, and processing history.
